messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: forward sampling RNG in place; need RStan update
parts:
Now that Peter's implementing the RNGs, I added
the ability to call random number generators in the
generated quantities block of a Stan program. For
example, to assign x to a unit normal random draw,
the code would be:

generated quantities {
real x;
x <- normal_rng(0,1);
}

I believe we decided to only allow RNG inside the generated
quantities block, because:

a. It doesn't make sense over params because we can't
take gradients, and

b. It's not clear it'd be useful in the transformed data
block, because transformed data's not saved anywhere.

Is this OK for a design? If not, now's the time to chime in.

If so, we can add the function signatures for the RNGs, add them
to the doc, and provide some examples.

It should make things like Gaussian process models faster
because we can use direct sampling instead of HMC for sampling-base
dinference.

I haven't enforced that constraint yet, but everything's in
place in the grammar to do so after some plumbing work.

I also needed to pass the random number generator through
the Stan command to the model's write_csv() and write_array() methods,
which are what execute the generated quantities block. So RStan is
going to need to do the same.

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] forward sampling RNG in place; need RStan update
parts:
On 3/8/13 11:41 AM, Jiqiang Guo wrote:
> Does this mean that when both write_array and write_csv are called (which could happen in RStan) the generated
> quantities are drawn twice?

Yes. You shouldn't call both write_array() and write_csv()
for a single sample. Why would you?

I should really replace the logic in write_csv() to first
call write_array(), but that's a separate issue that'll just
make the code a bit easier to maintain.

- Bob

A first priority is to get partial inits working. I hope

How important do people think having an inits block is?

we can generalize some of the current template metaprograms so
as not to have to write whole new functions for agrad::fvar types.

- Bob
